introduction: On this sixth Sunday of Easter, the apostles meet in Jerusalem and decide, with the Holy Spirit, not to burden the Gentile believers with more than is necessary. John sees the holy city coming down from heaven, lit by the glory of God. In the Gospel, Jesus promises the Holy Spirit and gives his peace: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Let us receive the peace of Christ.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Jesus gives us his peace and promises us the Holy Spirit. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church and her pastors: that, guided by the Holy Spirit, they may discern wisely and keep the Church in unity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace in the world, in our families and in our hearts: that Christ's peace may overcome every fear and division. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are troubled and afraid: that they may hear Jesus say, Do not let your hearts be troubled. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are preparing for Confirmation: that the Holy Spirit may teach them and remind them of all that Jesus said. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may love Jesus and keep his word, so that the Father and the Son may make their home in us. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son promised to send the Holy Spirit and to give us his peace. Make your home in us, and guide your Church in the way of truth. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: My peace I give to you
reflection.body:
The early Church faced a serious question: did Gentiles who became Christians have to become Jews first, and follow all of the law of Moses? The question caused "no small discord and discussion." So the apostles and elders met in Jerusalem. After prayer and debate, they sent a letter that begins with remarkable words: "For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us." They asked only a few essential things of the new believers. The Church learned to discern together, under the guidance of the Spirit.

In the Gospel, Jesus makes a promise to those who love him: "If a man loves me, he will keep my word. My Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him." God wants to live in us.

Jesus also promises the Holy Spirit: "the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you." The Spirit helps the Church remember and understand the words of Jesus in every age.

Then Jesus gives his disciples a parting gift: "Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don't let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful." His peace is not the absence of problems. It is his presence with us in the middle of them.

The Book of Revelation shows the goal: the holy city, where there is no temple, "for the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb are its temple," and no need of sun, "for the very glory of God illuminated it."

This week, when you feel troubled, stop and receive the peace of Christ. At Mass, when we offer one another a sign of peace, mean it.
